solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Horsewoman returning a bottle containing dodgy mixture

indicators.note: containing means the reversed pair holds the scrambled letters inside it
returning means the pair of pieces before it, a and the bottle, are read backwards

parts.note: a vial is a small bottle

indicators.note: a mixture is a jumble, so the letters of dodgy are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rider heading back with a bottle of some suspect concoction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses the pair, 'mixture' scrambles the dodgy letters, and 'containing' sets them in the middle; 'Horsewoman' is the legendary naked rider of Coventry.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Coventry noblewoman famously rode naked through the town on horseback, so she is the archetypal horsewoman.

clue.text: Get a load of paper to send up

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look, the same as get a load of
FT is the Financial Times, a newspaper

explanation.surface: An instruction to collect a pile of newspapers and ship them upstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word; 'send up' is the definition, not part of the surface's delivery job.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit or throw a ball high into the air is to send it up, as a golfer or cricketer does.

clue.text: Defeated artillerymen originally evacuated Ypres and Mons?

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letters of the two words before it
evacuated means emptied, so only the outside letters of Ypres remain

explanation.surface: A First World War picture: beaten gunners pulling out of the Belgian battlefields of Ypres and Mons.
explanation.walkthrough: Mons, a battle town, is the definition read as the plural of Mon, short for Monday; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: Mondays, abbreviated Mons, are examples of weekdays, hence the question mark for definition by example.

clue.text: After moving, girl at hand to pack up, finally

indicators.note: after moving means once the letters have been shifted about, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A girl, once moved, is at hand to help pack up at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole run 'girl at hand to' is the fodder, including 'to'; 'pack up' here means break down.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that packs up finally stops working completely, coming to a standstill.

clue.text: Party recalled our leading female cellist

parts.note: the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the reigning Queen, Britain's leading woman

explanation.surface: A political party summoning back Britain's foremost woman cellist.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is a Northern Irish political party; ER is the Queen. 'recalled' turns ER into RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacqueline du Pré was a celebrated English cellist famed for her Elgar concerto recording.

clue.text: Fair name? Appropriate in the case of a woman

parts.note: Vanity Fair, Thackeray's novel, is a name with Fair in it, so Vanity is the word that names the fair
to bag something is to appropriate or take it

explanation.surface: Musing on whether a fair name suits a woman's situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' looks like an adjective meaning just; it is the fair in Thackeray's title Vanity Fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A small handbag or case for cosmetics and a mirror, carried by a woman.

clue.text: Press person on latest news that's travelled fast

indicators.note: on means placed after, as the editor follows in an across clue

parts.note: SP stands for stop press, the latest news added to a paper
ED, short for editor, is a person in the press

explanation.surface: A journalist working on the latest story that has moved quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Stop press is the space in a newspaper for news arriving after printing began.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of speed: something that sped moved quickly.

clue.text: Background notes in the form of tweets?

definitions.text: Background notes in the form of tweets?

parts.words: Background notes in the form of tweets?
parts.note: background music played in shops, read as notes chirped by birds, whose song is piping

explanation.walkthrough: Tweets suggest social media, but they are birdsong; birds pipe, so their notes are piped.
explanation.definitionFit: Recorded music relayed through speakers in shops and lifts is heard as ambient sound behind other activity.

clue.text: Belittle unusual tip: no good for code breaking

parts.note: to decry is to belittle or disparage

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of tip appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: Dismissing a strange hint as useless for cracking a cipher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' makes PTI from TIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Converting an encrypted message back to plain text is the work of cracking a cipher.

clue.text: Escape paying extra for unauthorised dispatch

parts.note: to fly is to flee or escape
tipping is giving extra money for service

explanation.surface: Dodging a service charge as a way of sending something off without permission.
explanation.walkthrough: Fly-tipping is the British term for illegally dumping rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumping waste illegally on land is getting rid of it without permission.

clue.text: Pair helping one see incomplete requirement

indicators.note: incomplete means the last letter of the word is missing

parts.note: specs, short for spectacles, are a pair of glasses for seeing

explanation.surface: A pair of assistants for a seer who fall short of what is required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' drops the final S of SPECS.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for specification, a detailed statement of what is required.

clue.text: Paceman's length I recalled extremely unpredictable

parts.note: in cricket a quick is a fast bowler, a paceman; add the possessive S

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so length and I are read backwards

parts.note: very means extremely

explanation.surface: A cricket memory: a fast bowler's wildly erratic length.
explanation.walkthrough: A paceman is a fast bowler in cricket; 'recalled' turns L I into IL.
explanation.definitionFit: Like mercury, the liquid metal, something mercurial changes unexpectedly and cannot be pinned down.

clue.text: Church occasion created by commercial outlets — and in Germany, indeed!

parts.note: an ad is a commercial advertisement
vents are outlets for air or steam
und is the German word for and
ay, or aye, is an old affirmative meaning yes indeed

explanation.surface: A religious festival manufactured by shops, and in Germany too!
explanation.walkthrough: The surface jibes at commercialised Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: The first of the four Sundays before Christmas, opening the church year.

clue.text: Passing fifty-one volts through caused electrical malfunction

indicators.note: through means the voltage pieces pass inside the malfunction word

parts.note: a circuit that shorted had a short circuit
LI is 51 in Roman numerals
V is the symbol for volts

explanation.surface: Pushing fifty-one volts through a circuit made it fail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing' looks part of the electrical scene but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something passing lasts only a brief time, transient and fleeting.

clue.text: Play in dirty yard initially covering very small area

indicators.note: covering means the dirty word and the yard letter enclose the very piece

parts.note: unclean means dirty

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of yard

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area, small because shortened

explanation.surface: A tiny plot inside a filthy yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' means the dirty word wraps round the V; 'Play' looks like a verb but names a Chekhov drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Chekhov's 1898 drama about a disillusioned estate manager is a stage work.

clue.text: German host with a bishop following old carriage

indicators.note: following means the host and the rest come after the old letter

parts.note: Hans is a typical German man's name
an MC, master of ceremonies, is a host
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A German host with a bishop, both following an old carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old carriage' looks like the definition but 'old' gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-wheeled horse-drawn cab of the Victorian era, a kind of carriage for hire.

clue.text: Bar maybe doing its customers punch for sharing

parts.note: to clip someone is to punch or hit them
a joint is a cannabis cigarette passed round, or meat for sharing

explanation.surface: A pub serving its customers a punch to share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing' means cheating; 'punch' is not the drink but a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub or bar that overcharges or swindles its patrons, a slang term.

clue.text: Living way east of wine-producing region

indicators.note: east of means to the right of, after, in an across entry

parts.note: a cru is a vineyard or wine-growing area in France
ST, short for street, is a way

explanation.surface: A dwelling spot located east of a vineyard region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Living' looks like a verb but is a noun, as in earning a living.
explanation.definitionFit: Earning one's crust is earning a living, from crust as bread, basic sustenance.

clue.text: Chap's moral philosophy greatly diminished

indicators.note: greatly diminished means much is cut away from the phrase, leaving a short run from its middle

explanation.surface: A man whose ethical outlook has shrunk dramatically.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is a link for is; the letters span moRAL PHilosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: A common masculine first name, so an example of a fellow.

clue.text: Consumption of one interfering with Scandinavian girl's weight

parts.note: Inge is a Scandinavian girl's name, with the possessive S

indicators.note: interfering with means getting in among, so the one goes inside the weight

parts.note: a ton is a unit of weight
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone meddling with a Nordic girl's weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumption' is eating, not the old word for tuberculosis.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking food or drink into the body is eating, the act of consuming.

clue.text: Smashing large bully, by Jove, all over the place!

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A big bully thrashing about, by Jove, everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' signals the rearrangement. The phrase is London slang popularised by Del Boy in the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheerful slang exclamation meaning excellent or wonderful.

clue.text: Person nibbling tart half-heartedly

indicators.note: half-heartedly means half the central pair of letters is lost

parts.note: tart and bitter both mean sharp-tasting

explanation.surface: Someone nibbling a pastry without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' looks like a pastry but means sour; one of its middle Ts goes.
explanation.definitionFit: One who nibbles takes small bites, so is one who bites.

clue.text: Spare top is pinched from wood

indicators.note: top is pinched from means the first letter is stolen from the word below it in a down entry

parts.note: ebony is a dense black wood

explanation.surface: Someone stealing a spare top from a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare' means lean, not extra.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare build is lean and thin, with the skeleton showing.

clue.text: The girl in row five standing up?

indicators.note: standing up means upended, read upwards in a down entry

parts.note: a din is a noisy row
E is the fifth letter, so row E is the fifth row in a theatre

explanation.surface: Spotting a girl standing up in the fifth row of a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word; theatre rows are lettered, so row five is row E.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: Blade going round front and back of knife

parts.note: the van is the front, as in vanguard

indicators.note: back of means the final letter of knife

explanation.surface: A sword or knife being spun, front to back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blade going round' is the whole definition, as in a windmill or turbine.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating sail or flat paddle of a windmill or turbine, turning in wind or flow.

clue.text: Outlaw can, if put on spot

indicators.note: put on means placed after, in an across entry

parts.note: a spot is a little bit
can and john are both slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: An outlaw could be put on the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood's giant companion was a member of his band of outlaws in Sherwood Forest.

clue.text: Tar on road turned grey

indicators.note: on means placed after, in an across entry
turned means flipped around so the letters run backwards

parts.note: an AB, able seaman, is a sailor, as is a tar

explanation.surface: Tar spread on a road went grey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tar' is a sailor, not the road surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull and lacking colour, as a dun or dreary tone is.

clue.text: Unduly optimistic son to stay and watch daughter

parts.note: to tarry is to stay or linger
to eye is to watch

explanation.surface: A hopeful son staying to watch his daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: S, son, and D, daughter, are standard family abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamily idealistic, naively seeing things as better than they are.
